Operating margin fell from **16.7% in 1924 to 6.7% in 1927**, recovered to **15.6% in 1928**, then slipped to **10.8% in 1929**. In that last season, the cooperative sold 80 more crates, but operating costs rose by 750 crowns while revenue rose by only 306.

The rebound followed the sorter’s late-1927 arrival. The annual accounts cannot isolate its contribution, distinguish changes in variety mix, or establish equipment payback.

- [Board brief](<TEMP>/tmpas6byfg5/board-brief.html) — an offline report explaining the six-season trend.
- [Season ledger](<TEMP>/tmpas6byfg5/season-accounts.csv) — all six source rows and 30 verified calculations, with formulas defined in the brief.

The [board brief](<TEMP>/tmppj640ky0/orchard-board-brief.html) shows that operating margin fell from 16.67% in 1924 to 6.72% in 1927, recovered to 15.62% in 1928, then slipped to 10.84% in 1929 despite record crate sales.

Lower recorded operating cost per crate was the largest contributor to the 1928 surplus recovery. The accounts establish that the recovery followed the sorter’s arrival, but they cannot isolate its effect or establish its payback.


The checker reports a 15-minute overlap between shelving and story hour, accepts the back-to-back handoff at 10:30, and flags `10:75` on line 6 with the expected time format.
